body.notes: Checked the proof in claimset-code/half-moments/proofs/properties.md, section H4, with the Notation block and Lemma 0, against TM1/TM3. (1) Lemma 0: a finite mean gives E|D| finite and E[D]=0, so E[D+]=E[D-]=delta; not constant (not almost surely constant) gives P(D!=0)>0, so E|D|=2*delta>0, and E[D+]>0 forces P(D>0)>0, likewise P(D<0)>0. Holds. (2) R=E[D+^0.5]>0 and I>0, since each integrand is non-negative and strictly positive on a set of positive probability; both finite by Jensen (E|D|^0.5 <= (E|D|)^0.5). Holds. (3) With R>0, Arg(R+iI)=arctan(I/R), in (0, pi/2). Holds. (4) Subtraction formula arctan 1 - arctan t = arctan((1-t)/(1+t)) is valid for t>-1, here t=I/R>0; (1-t)/(1+t)=(R-I)/(R+I), so A = 1 - phi/(pi/4) = (4/pi) arctan((R-I)/(R+I)), which agrees with both forms in TM3. Holds. (5) R,I>0 give |R-I|<R+I strictly, so the argument is in (-1,1); arctan is strictly increasing with arctan(+-1)=+-pi/4, so A is in the open interval (-1,1). Holds. (6) arctan is odd and strictly increasing with arctan 0 = 0, so A=0 iff R=I and A<0 iff I>R; both directions follow. The proof says 'increasing' where strict monotonicity is what is used; arctan is strictly increasing, so nothing is missing. The remark that +-1 is not attained is consistent with (2). Numeric check of my own (not a proof): 200000 random discrete distributions with 2 to 5 points; the two forms of A agree to 4e-16 and the sign and zero conditions held in all cases; 3 cases gave A=1.0 in double precision with I/R below 1e-18, and at 60 digits these are below 1 (rounding, not counterexamples). Two-point distributions with mass eps at the upper point give A = -0.9597, -0.99873, -0.9999987 for eps = 1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-12: the bound is approached and not reached, so the open interval cannot be narrowed. Nothing wrong or missing found; the statement as worded follows for the population coefficient, and for the sample coefficient as the empirical distribution of a sample that is not all equal.
